title: Oncall: Traffic Sculpting & Credential-flood Scratchpad
body:
Purpose
Quick, messy notes from an oncall surface where we saw a sustained credential-based flood hitting the hosted inference API. This is a scratchpad for signals, immediate mitigations we tried, quick queries, and follow-ups. Not a final runbook — draft for iteration.

Context / Incident summary
- Date/time window: 2026-02-14 09:40 UTC -> ongoing when notes taken (brief lull at 10:20 UTC).
- Observed behavior: large burst of low-cost token generation requests across dozens of API keys (many small sessions), sharp rise in 429s across frontdoors once internal queueing filled. Traffic pattern: extremely high new-session rate, low tokens/session (2–6 tokens), mostly text-generation endpoint /v1/complete.
- Hypothesis: leaked API keys or compromised client (bot farm) attempting credential stuffing to find cheap completions. Not a single account spike, distributed across keys; correlated with new-account signup churn earlier in the week.

Primary impacts
- Elevated latency for normal traffic as autoscale struggled to keep up with many tiny sessions.
- Billing anomalies: small token per request but high request count causing quota exhaustion for some reserved pools.
- Customer complaints about intermittent 429s and timeouts.

Immediate detection signals used
- API gateway metrics: requests/min by key, new-session rate, 95th latency.
- Auth service: sudden bump in key validation events flagged > X requests/min per key.
- WAF logs: repeated identical UA strings and HTTP header shapes.
- Console alert: quota consumption rate alert (threshold: 120% of expected per-hour).

Quick mitigation steps attempted (timeline)
- 09:45 UTC: raised global soft throttling on the public frontdoor (temporarily reduced per-ip token bucket from 50r/s -> 10r/s). Observed slight reduction in overall throughput but collateral impact on legitimate customers in shared NAT environments.
- 09:50 UTC: enabled a trial WAF rule to block requests with empty/referrer-less origins + suspicious UA fingerprint (rule id tmp-cred-flood-1). This dropped ~28% of offending requests but introduced some false positives for CLI SDK traffic.
- 09:58 UTC: rolled an allowlist for identified Partner IP ranges to avoid blocking known customers.
- 10:05 UTC: aggressively lowered per-key burst tokens for keys that exceeded 60 req/min for more than 2 minutes (programmatic throttling). This reduced resource churn but highlighted that many attacker keys were newly minted so per-account heuristics were weak.
- 10:18 UTC: started coordinated key rotation for a subset of accounts suspected of leakage (manual outreach + rotate-change in console). Requires CS involvement for verified customers.

Root-cause hypotheses to validate
- Keys leaked via a bulk third-party integration that stored keys in plaintext (check tickets and partner onboarding logs).
- Automated account creation churned through free-tier trials; bot farm used account creation to obtain fresh keys. (Check signup IP distribution + device fingerprinting).
- Credential stuffing using previously breached credential sets — cross-check email hashes and signup timestamps.

Useful queries / commands (copyable)
- Top-keys by RPS in last 15m: SELECT key, sum(requests) FROM gateway_metrics WHERE ts > now()-15m GROUP BY key ORDER BY sum DESC LIMIT 200
- New-session spike check: filter where session_length < 8 tokens AND requests > 100 in 15m; correlate with created_at within last 48h.
- WAF fingerprint aggregate: count by user_agent, header_signature, geo.
- Identify NAT clusters: group by source_ip_prefix (e.g., /24) to spot cloud provider blasts.

Observed signal patterns worth noting
- UA string shared by ~62% of offending requests: 'curl/7.88.1 (ssl)'. Many attackers used simple CURL.
- Header signature: missing Accept-Language and missing Referer in most cases.
- Geo: broad distribution but heavy in a few cloud provider ranges.
- Timing: periodic bursts every 3 minutes for 10–12 minutes, then pause.

Recommended short-term playbook (actionable)
1) Tiered quota slicing: carve the public pool into short-lived micro-quotas (e.g., 1000 req/day per key default for new keys) and require verification to raise. Implement via config flag new-account-default-throttle = true.
2) Fast key cooling: automatic suspend for keys that show > 200 requests in 10 minutes and session_token_rate < 8 tokens/session (pattern of low-token flood). Notify owner and require rotation.
3) WAF adjustments: convert tmp-cred-flood-1 from block -> challenge (captcha or JS challenge) for ambiguous traffic. Keep block for high-confidence signatures.
4) IP reputation: feed cloud provider ASN blocks matching observed bursts into a temporary rate-limiter (not full block) to reduce hammering while avoiding collateral damage.
5) Signup verification hardening: enable throttle/recaptcha for account creation from high-risk IP ranges.

Longer-term engineering follow-ups
- Implement per-key session smoothing: incentivize longer session reuse by making short sessions more expensive (billing or token pricing tweak).
- Revise default quota provisioning for new accounts: lower by default, then auto-increase based on real usage signal and verification progress.
- Improve key lifecycle APIs: bulk rotate, programmatic revoke with dry-run to estimate affected customers.
- Automated anomaly scoring: train a lightweight model to score keys by abnormality (newness, request shape, UA, geo entropy). Integrate into routing to push suspicious keys to lower-cost/burst lanes.
- Observability: add a dashboard with per-key churn heatmap and a 'new keys by minute' heatline.

Customer communication notes
- For impacted customers who see increased 429s: be explicit that we're mitigating an abuse event that may temporarily affect shared pools; offer to migrate them to Dedicated for isolation, or to generate a rotated key with priority recovery.
- CS playbook: when rotating keys, include a sample script to replace key across SDKs and instructions for in-place rotation to avoid breaking production.

Follow-ups / open questions
- Which onboarding partners accepted raw keys during signup flow? (Ask product-engineering to audit onboarding connectors)
- Can billing team provide a quick script to detect customers whose monthly cost jumped due to repeated short-session spam?
- Is there appetite for a short-term paid rate-limit protection add-on to offer to high-value customers while we harden defaults?

Post-incident items for next retro
- Evaluate false positives caused by tmp-cred-flood-1 (who was impacted, how many tickets).
- Measure efficacy of per-key burst reduction: did backend P95 improve? Track over 72h.
- Decide threshold for automatic account verification before quota increases.

Appendix: quick snippets for CS to rotate keys (example)
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/keys/rotate -H 'Authorization: Bearer OLD_KEY' -d '{"rotate":true}'
- SDK note: recommend implementing key lookup via env var + fallback list to allow swap without restart.

Raw notes / things I scribbled during the event
- Miguel: try a JS challenge for UA curl/7.* only, but that'll catch non-browsers.
- Priya: block list was too aggressive; add allowlist for partner ranges first.
- Thomas: add a new dashboard tile for "new keys per minute" stat.
- Rhea: can security run quick sweep of partner integrations for plaintext key storage?

Status: draft — will refine after check-ins with product onboarding, CS, and infra.

End of scratchpad.
